anchor: The heavenly Rayes or Influences
statement: The printed Hermes section attributes bodily conditions from conception and birth to planetary influences and zodiacal signs; Aries is given the head.
conditions: Conception or nativity, not a specific illness enquiry.
limits: No ancient original or independent empirical corroboration verified.

anchor: The right Eye to the Sun
statement: The printed correspondence table assigns right eye to Sun, left eye to Moon, hearing and ears to Saturn, brain to Jupiter, blood to Mars, smell and taste to Venus, and tongue/food-pipe or throat/lung-pipe to Mercury.
conditions: Table is a collection of assignments, not separate observations.
limits: Preserve the gender-independent right/left eye assignment here instead of silently replacing it with older context-sensitive rules.

anchor: That member suffers a defect
statement: An afflicted planet said to signify or govern a member at conception or birth is alleged to impair that member.
conditions: Planet must be afflicted and assigned to the relevant body part.
limits: Does not determine condition severity or supply individual cases.

anchor: the Head, the Breast, the Hands, and Feet
statement: Head, breast, hands and feet are separately called principal parts, and the author extends affliction from their governing planet to all or part of the assigned member.
conditions: Governor said to be unfortunate at conception or birth.
limits: No complete assignment of all four to specific planets supplied here.

anchor: when the Sun or Moone be ill disposed
statement: The author gives eye examples for Sun or Moon, hearing/ear/teeth examples for Saturn and speech/tongue examples for Mercury; internal organs and fingers/nails are also considered.
conditions: Afflicted or oppressed assigned body-governing planet.
limits: May overlap preceding general correspondence, not an independent case.

anchor: Planets of contrary nature and power
statement: Within the historical humoral framework, curative medicines are described as contrary in nature to the planet alleged to afflict a body part.
conditions: A curable defect within the source's framework.
limits: Not modern clinical or treatment advice.

anchor: To Saturn are assigned such Medicaments
statement: Saturn is assigned cooling, drying and attenuating medicaments.
limits: Do not infer pharmacological actions or clinical safety.

anchor: To Mercury such as congeale
statement: Mercury is associated with substances said to congeal and be flatulent or windy.
limits: The wording is a planetary classification, not a modern efficacy estimate.

anchor: To Mars such as are calefactive
statement: Mars is assigned warming/heating and filling medicines, with rhetoric concerning blood.
limits: No dosage, clinical testing or verified benefit.

anchor: To Jupiter and Venus things conglutinating
statement: Jupiter and Venus are associated with closing, softening medicines described as alleviating ulcers.
limits: Specific drugs and treatment outcomes are not tested here.

anchor: The Moone helps that Planet
statement: The Moon is said to aid the planet to which she applies whether that planet is good or bad.
limits: Aid is not explicitly a good outcome; preserve the good-or-bad qualifier.

anchor: set or erected for the houre of his first falling sick
statement: The source asks the practitioner to erect a chart for first falling ill or lying down and examine positions and mutual planetary conditions.
limits: Historical method; the subsequent universal healing rhetoric is an author assertion, not validation.

anchor: if the certaine hour of the parties first falling sick
statement: When the certain illness-onset hour cannot be obtained, use the time the physician is first asked for judgment, attending to the Moon's prior and subsequent aspects.
conditions: Onset time unavailable, not merely inconvenient.
limits: Not the identical time hierarchy of all prior sixth-house passages; this is local.

anchor: from whom the Moone is separated
statement: The practitioner is told to inspect lunar separation and application, conjunction, square and opposition. Malefic configuration is associated with protracted severe illness; fortunes with faster remedy.
limits: No independent illness outcome or calibrated prognosis.

anchor: swift in motion, and encreasing in light
statement: Moon speed and increase in light are treated separately, including their coincidence or absence; subsequent adversity can override earlier favourable timing.
conditions: Known lunar speed and lunar illumination change.
limits: Do not substitute one variable for the other.

anchor: after her conjunction with the Sun
statement: The text links a particular post-conjunction path to an adverse Mars aspect before opposition to Sun with no intervening benefic aspect to a fatal prognosis.
conditions: Lunar light and motion increasing in the narrated sequence
Square or opposition to Mars before opposition to Sun
limits: The narrow combined conditions cannot be reduced to any Mars square.

section: Benefic exception to adverse lunar path
anchor: but if conjoyned, or in good aspect
statement: A benefic conjunction or favourable aspect is described as a recovery exception despite a prior expectation of non-survival.
conditions: Benefic relation as specified in original local sentence.
limits: The pronoun and temporal scope are compact; leave unresolved if not source-determined.

anchor: decreasing in light and motion
statement: A waning slow Moon in square or opposition to Saturn is associated with a severe or fatal illness, except where the disease's vigour immediately remits after the Saturn opposition; benefic application is another favourable alternative.
limits: Immediate-remission and benefic exceptions must be retained.

anchor: during the encrease of the Moone in number and light
statement: The author reports that illness increases with Moon's increase in number and light, but diminishes when the Moon grows slow.
limits: 'Number' lacks a normalized technical definition in this passage; not an executable rate equation.

anchor: malignant influence of Saturn or Mercury
statement: The author connects Saturn or Mercury configurations to a cold, somnolent, withdrawn symptom cluster and proposes hot medicines in that historical framework.
conditions: Oppressed by Saturn or Mercury at first lying down.
limits: No modern diagnosis or safe drug inference.

anchor: malevolent configuration of the Sun or Mars
statement: Sun or Mars configurations are linked to feverish, agitated, heated symptoms; the historical proposed responses include bloodletting, purging or cooling.
conditions: Unfavourable Sun or Mars configurations at first lying down.
limits: Bloodletting and purging are unvalidated historical treatment suggestions; not recommended.

anchor: What Medicines are agreeable to the nature of Mars
statement: The text contrasts heating/softening substances with cooling, binding or repressing ones, and relates their purported opposition to planetary causes.
limits: Potential internal inconsistency around attribution of organ diseases to Sun/Mars versus Saturn/Mercury must not be silently corrected.

anchor: of which sort are these
statement: A three-column catalogue of historical cooling/refrigerating medicines is given.
limits: A list of materia medica is not proof of effectiveness or safety. Some listed substances are toxic. Preserve source spelling and unresolved readings in a separate table.

anchor: Such Medicines as are naturally calefactive or hot
statement: A three-column historical heating/cale-factive materia medica catalogue continues across the page boundary.
limits: List can include unsafe or poisonous items; no use instructions or doses should be derived.

section: Opposite remedial qualities for putative sources
anchor: To expulse and recover those Diseases
statement: The text advocates heating and softening for ills ascribed to Saturn or Mercury, and cooling/repressing for those ascribed to Sun or Mars.
conditions: Planetary cause has first been assigned from the lunar course.
limits: Medical recommendation is historical only, not fit for patient care.

anchor: the Moone decreasing in light and motion
statement: Introduces the twelve-sign catalogue for the Moon decreasing in light and motion and afflicted by Saturn through conjunction, square or opposition at initial decumbiture or first question.
conditions: Moon in one of the twelve signs
limits: Each sign row inherits this stated scope; no invented aspect orb.
